title: Quantum-advantage resource of a two-mode Gaussian state: Analytical theory of convex optimization and a Galois no-go for the closed-form solution
abstract: We study the problem of extracting a quantum complexity resource from a mixed Gaussian state of the multimode light. We present the first complete, certificate-checked solution to this problem in a genuinely coupled sector. We carry this out for the two-mode case, the smallest case in which modes are genuinely coupled. Even in this case the solution is highly nontrivial, and we rigorously prove that it cannot be given in a closed form.
summary: The paper rigorously analyzes the quantum-advantage resource of two-mode Gaussian light by solving a constrained convex optimization problem. It establishes that while simple cases yield closed forms, the generic case for coupled modes leads to an optimal value determined by the least real root of a degree-12 polynomial. This demonstrates a fundamental mathematical barrier to finding general analytical solutions in this quantum regime.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the 'quantum-advantage resource' of a mixed Gaussian state, which requires solving a complex convex optimization problem.
main_result: For generic two-mode states with genuinely coupled modes, the optimal quantum-advantage resource cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions or radicals due to an algebraic obstruction related to the Galois group $S_{12}$.
method: The authors use convex optimization techniques, formulating the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) and solving it by reducing it to maximizing a dual concave cost function.
model_or_system: The system models multimode light described by its quadrature covariance matrix $V$. The focus is on the two-mode case ($M=2$), which represents the smallest regime exhibiting genuinely coupled modes.
key_observables: Quantum-advantage resource, $N_q(V)$, defined as $ rac{1}{2}(	ext{Tr} V_{\star q} - 2)$; the optimal covariance matrix $V_{\star q}$.
important_parameters: The number of nonclassical directions ($\kappa$); compatibility between eigenvectors; and the structure of the polynomial whose root determines $N_q(V)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on reducing the SDP to a dual problem, and closed-form solutions are only possible when the system falls into specific 'decoupled strata' where eigenvector compatibility holds.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the structure is built around deriving polynomial equations whose roots determine the resource value.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the optimization problem (primal/dual), establishing an oracle formula for the minimizer, analyzing specific low-$\kappa$ cases ($\kappa=0, 1$), and culminating in the general result that requires solving a degree-12 polynomial equation for coupled systems.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical insight into resource quantification in continuous variable quantum optics, establishing rigorous boundaries on what can be solved analytically versus what requires numerical methods.
